relations.note: Ayido-Hwedo transports Mawu-Lisa during creation and later supports the completed earth.
At Mawu's request, Ayido-Hwedo coils beneath the overburdened earth to support it.
Danbala and Ayida are paired as husband and wife in many Haitian traditions.
Some traditions treat Danbala and Ayida as dual aspects of one serpent principle.
Some Haitian lineages describe Erzulie Freda as Damballah's lover or concubine.
Haitian iconography represents Danbala through Saint Patrick because the saint's images include snakes.
relations.source: Desmangles, The Faces of the Gods

relations.note: Moses' serpent staff and bronze serpent support a localized identification with Danbala.
Borderland and Brazilian systems equate or juxtapose Dan with the Yoruba-Nago rainbow serpent.
Missionary and colonial polemic identified Dangbé with the biblical serpent or Satan.
Later Louisiana interpretation associates the sacred-serpent title with Danbala, though historical equivalence remains unproved.
